objectives: Evaluate abdominal pain with danger-sign screening before presumptive deworming.
Identify when empiric helminth treatment is appropriate by age and symptom pattern.
Provide hygiene and follow-up advice to reduce reinfection and missed severe disease.
takeaways: Most worm-related abdominal pain is outpatient-manageable when severe danger signs are absent.
Albendazole use should match age eligibility and local deworming guidance.
Counseling on hand hygiene, footwear, and sanitation is part of treatment.
learnCaseOverrides.blurb: A school-age child with abdominal pain and poor appetite is brought for 'worm medicine'. Avoid reflex treatment without screening.

sections.title: Chief complaint
sections.text: Intermittent abdominal pain and reduced appetite

sections.title: Caregiver request
sections.text: Parent asks directly for deworming tablets after seeing worms in stool once.

coach.title: Paul is uncomfortable but active
coach.body: First confirm there are no red flags that require referral-level workup.

coach.title: What does this allow you to do safely?
coach.body: Use findings to decide outpatient vs urgent referral.

options.text: Stable child with likely helminth-related symptoms; outpatient management is appropriate
Immediate surgical abdomen requiring emergency transfer
No need to examine because caregiver already diagnosed worms
Treat as severe malaria despite no fever pattern

question.right: Correct. Without red flags, this is suitable for outpatient management and age-appropriate deworming decisions.
question.wrong: Skipping exam or over-escalating without danger signs leads to poor resource use and missed teaching.

sections.title: Treatment option
sections.detail: Single-dose deworming per guideline plus dietary/hygiene counseling

sections.title: Context
sections.text: Child is 6 years old, attends school barefoot at times, and has poor handwashing access.

coach.title: Pick the most appropriate management package

options.text: Give age-appropriate albendazole and reinforce sanitation, footwear, and hand hygiene
Start broad-spectrum antibiotics for all abdominal pain
Withhold all treatment because worms are always self-limiting
Give repeated deworming doses daily for one week without indication

question.right: Correct. In a stable 6-year-old with compatible symptoms, guideline-based deworming and prevention counseling are appropriate.
question.wrong: Non-targeted antibiotics or incorrect dosing strategies are common but avoidable errors in worm-related complaints.

sections.title: Case outcome
sections.text: You ruled out danger signs, used age-appropriate deworming, and gave prevention counseling.
sections.emphasis: Abdominal complaints need triage before presumptive treatment.

coach.title: Key teaching points
coach.body: Caregiver expectations often push immediate deworming. Safe HC III practice still starts with danger-screening, then targeted treatment and hygiene counseling.
